title: Stock Futures Edge Lower After Slide As Nvidia Turmoil Weighs On AI Trade
excerpt: Nasdaq futures led early declines on Friday after Nvidia fell 4.3% on Jensen Huang's exit, with oil above $95 and producer price data next.
body:
• US stock futures edged lower early Friday after Thursday's slide, with Nasdaq-100 futures down between 0.11% and 0.36% across early reports, as investors assessed Nvidia's leadership turmoil.
  • Nvidia fell 4.3% on Thursday after CEO Jensen Huang stepped down; CFO Colette Kress will lead as interim CEO, and analysts told CNBC a further 20% correction was possible - an expectation, not a result.
  • Brent crude settled up more than 3% at $95.82 a barrel on Thursday, adding pressure, while October producer prices were the next data point, with economists polled by Dow Jones expecting a 0.4% monthly rise.
  • Reader utility: despite the slide, the Nasdaq was up 3.2% for the week and the S&P 500 on pace for a 2.9% gain in the CNBC update - futures moves this small signal caution, not a confirmed reversal.

US stock futures edged lower early on Friday, November 13, after the major indexes slid in Thursday's regular session amid turmoil at Nvidia. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average were down 0.09%, S&P 500 futures were down 0.14% and Nasdaq-100 futures fell 0.36% in the CNBC live update carried by AmeriLedger. A later Reuters snapshot at 5:03 a.m. ET showed a mixed picture, with Dow E-minis up 98 points, or 0.19%, S&P 500 E-minis up 9.75 points, or 0.13%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis still down 31 points, or 0.11%.

What moved on Thursday

The Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 each dropped about 0.4% in regular trading, and the Dow slid almost 190 points, or 0.4%. Nvidia's 4.3% decline dragged on all three averages, even as the stock ended off its lows. On Thursday, Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive following reported extramarital affairs, including a relationship with a woman US intelligence officials believe is a Chinese spy, according to the CNBC update. Chief financial officer Colette Kress, at the company for more than a decade, will lead as interim CEO while the board looks internally and externally for a permanent replacement.

Reuters reported Nvidia shares rose 1.8% in Friday premarket trading after losing around 11% for the week through Thursday, while remaining on course for their longest streak of weekly losses since October 2012. Several chip peers were lower in premarket trade, with AMD and Broadcom each down more than 2.5%, Reuters said. Analysts told CNBC that Huang's exit could trigger a 20% correction in the stock; that is an analyst expectation reported by CNBC, not a market outcome.

"I'm a bear for AI-related stocks. You've got to exit these waves before they crash. And in AI, we've got a big wave going on."

- Sean Peche, Founder and Portfolio Manager, Ranmore Fund Management, to Reuters

Oil, Microsoft and the data ahead

Oil kept pressure on equities. Brent crude rose more than 3% on Thursday to settle at $95.82 a barrel after President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post, "We don't need a deal with Iran," raising concern the US-Iran conflict could drag on. Microsoft was a separate drag on Friday: Reuters reported its Outlook, Teams and Copilot services were down in an outage stretching beyond 12 hours, and its shares fell 2.6% in premarket trading.

The next catalyst is October's producer price index, a measure of wholesale inflation. Economists polled by Dow Jones expect headline PPI to rise 0.4% on the month and 6.6% from a year earlier, according to the CNBC update. Reuters reported traders are fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike next month, with odds of a 50 basis point increase around 12% on the CME FedWatch tool against a widely expected 25 basis point move - market pricing and expectations, not a Fed decision. Even after Thursday's fall, the major averages were heading for weekly advances and their best weekly performances since early August, the CNBC update said.
